title: Almerys TP for opticians: professional portal, coverage approval, statuses, and payment
keywordCluster: www almerys com creer mon compte
metaDescription: Almerys TP for opticians: professional portal access, optical coverage approval, 8 statuses explained, payment, and contacts. How to log in on almerys.com.
contentHtml:
Almerys TP is handled on almerys.com, in the “Site des PEC” (coverage approval site): the optician under agreement submits quotes and coverage requests there, one piece of equipment per request. Almerys is an operator that processes coverage approvals on behalf of supplementary health insurers. To access it, you must be under agreement and validate your account. You then log in with a login ID, a password, and a one-time code received by email. After that, it is the status shown in the portal history, not the quote, that tells you where the file stands.

Key points
  • Almerys is a third-party payment operator, not a care network: a supplementary health insurer (mutuelle) can pair it with a separate network.
  • The professional portal is on almerys.com, in the Site des PEC.
  • Access takes three steps: network agreement, account validation, then login with a 6-digit code received by email.
  • A request covers only one piece of equipment, entered by LPP codes (the supplier code for lenses). The “Valoriser” (Price) button assigns the coverage approval (PEC) number and displays the amounts.
  • The portal history has eight states. Only “Validée” (Approved) authorizes you to deliver the equipment and then bill.
  • Almerys does not publish a payment time on its professional pages: track the change from “Facturée” (Billed) to “Soldée” (Settled) and check the amount received.

What is Almerys TP and which supplementary health insurers use it?

Almerys is a third-party payment (tiers payant: the patient pays nothing upfront, insurers pay the provider directly) operator: it manages third-party payment on behalf of supplementary insurers: insurance companies, mutuelles, and social protection groups.

A third-party payment operator is the intermediary that receives the optician's coverage requests and invoices on behalf of the supplementary insurance (AMC). The AMC is the customer's supplementary health insurance: their mutuelle or insurer. Do not confuse it with a care network, which is a separate arrangement chosen by the supplementary insurer. Example: the mutuelles of Aéma Groupe (Aésio mutuelle, Apivia Macif Mutuelle, MNFCT…) use Almerys for third-party payment, according to Acuité. Their care network is Carte Blanche Partenaires. In practice, for the same customer, you may deal with Almerys for the coverage approval and with another player for the network terms.

Almerys is not a newcomer for opticians. In 2017, Acuité reported that 11,000 professionals used its third-generation third-party payment. This figure is old: it gives an idea of the operator's footprint, not its current size.

The Almerys portal has no insurer selector: the supplementary insurer appears once the beneficiary is found.

The right habit: read the customer's third-party payment card before entering anything. The supplementary insurer's name is on it. That is where to direct a customer who has a complaint. According to the Almerys healthcare professionals page, the operator does not handle complaints from policyholders.

To place Almerys among the other third-party payment portals, the parent page covers the platforms an optical store deals with.

How do you access the Almerys professional portal?

The Almerys professional portal, on almerys.com, opens in three steps: sign the network agreement, validate your account following the instructions sent by Almerys, then log in. The account only opens after the network agreement: there is no point trying to create it before.

According to the professional portal login page, you must be under agreement with Almerys and have validated your account to access it. The full process takes five steps:

  1. Send the network agreement request. Send a crossed-out claim form or your local health insurance office (CPAM) certificate to celluleconventionnementalmerys@almerys.com.
  2. Wait for the email from Almerys. It gives the instructions for validating your account.
  3. Validate the account. Follow these instructions to the letter, otherwise you will not be able to log in.
  4. Log in to the professional portal. Use the store's login ID and password.
  5. Work on the Site des PEC. That is where quotes and coverage requests are submitted.

Logging in: login ID, password, and one-time code

Each store logs in with its login ID and password, then enters a 6-digit one-time code sent by email, at every login. This is what our agents record on the portal. In practice, the person at the counter needs access to the mailbox that receives this code at the moment they log in.

In a store where several team members handle third-party payment, settle this point once and for all. Which address receives the code? Who can check it? What happens when the account holder is away? Without this, an urgent request can wait simply because nobody sees the code come in.

Creating your account, forgotten password, or locked account

The account is created by following the instructions received from Almerys after the network agreement. The professional pages we reviewed do not detail the password reset procedure. For any account problem, the dedicated address is the network agreement unit's, given in the contact section.

How do you submit an optical coverage request on Almerys?

An Almerys optical coverage approval is handled on the “Site des PEC”. You find the beneficiary and choose a quote or a coverage request. You enter each item by its LPP code, then click “Valoriser”. The PEC (coverage approval) is the supplementary insurer's agreement on the amount it will pay directly to the store.

The LPP code is the code from the list of reimbursable products and services, the classification that identifies each frame and each lens. On Almerys, our agents record this sequence:

  1. Log in to the Site des PEC. Login ID, password, then the code received by email.
  2. Find the beneficiary. The supplementary insurer appears once the beneficiary is found, with no list of insurers to browse.
  3. Choose the request type. An optical request can be a quote or a coverage request.
  4. Enter the equipment by LPP codes. Frame and lenses, each item with its code. For lenses, it is the supplier code.
  5. Click “Valoriser”. The request is created, a PEC number is assigned, and the amounts are displayed.
  6. Track the status in the history. It tells you whether you can deliver.

Only one piece of equipment per request

An Almerys request covers only one piece of equipment. If the customer takes a second pair, you need a second request, with its own PEC number. Keep both numbers in the customer file: you will use them to track each approval, each invoice, and each payment separately.

The trap: forgetting that, for lenses, it is the supplier code. Check it on the purchase order before pricing.

Which documents should you attach?

Almerys does not publish a list of documents: attach what the portal asks for and keep the prescription and quote in the file.

One request per piece of equipment, a code to enter at every login, a status to watch: on a busy Saturday, these steps add up quickly. That is what Granit's agents do: they enter the requests on the Almerys Site des PEC. They then send the PEC number and the status back to the store team. To review the whole chain, from request to payment, also read our guide third-party payment for opticians: from coverage approval to collection.

What do the statuses of an Almerys coverage approval mean?

The portal history displays eight possible states, recorded by our agents: Créée (Created), En instance (Under review), Validée (Approved), Refusée (Rejected), Périmée (Expired), Annulée (Canceled), Facturée (Billed), and Soldée (Settled).

The status that matters before delivering is “Validée”: the supplementary insurer accepts the coverage approval. “Créée” only means the request is recorded, with no decision. “En instance” means it is still under review. In both cases, the equipment must not leave the store on the strength of the quote alone.

Once the equipment is delivered and the invoice sent, the request changes to “Facturée”. The file is closed when it shows “Soldée”: it is paid, and you still need to check that the amount received matches the priced amount.

Three statuses require a new request. “Refusée”: no coverage approval as it stands, you need to read the reason, correct, then start again. “Périmée”: the approval has passed its validity period, which the pages we reviewed do not specify. “Annulée”: the request is no longer active, and you need to submit a new one if the equipment is still being delivered.

Stuck on Almerys?

Start from the symptom you see on screen: each case below tells you where to check, what to do, and who to turn to.

I can't find the insurer in the list

On Almerys, there is no list of insurers to browse: the supplementary insurer appears once the beneficiary is found. If nothing appears, go back to the customer's third-party payment card. Check that it does mention Almerys and that it is still valid. Then check the information entered to find the beneficiary. If the card points to another operator, the request is made on that operator's portal, for example on the Viamedis professional portal. If doubt persists, call the healthcare professionals service (see the contact section).

The coverage request is rejected

First read the reason shown in the history. Then check the points specific to Almerys: only one piece of equipment per request, each item entered by its LPP code, the supplier code for lenses. Correct, then submit a new request: a rejected request does not turn into an approval. If the reason seems related to the customer's coverage rights, their supplementary insurer, whose name is on the card, can clarify it.

It stays pending, with no response

A request that is “Créée” or “En instance” does not have a decision yet. Almerys does not publish a response time for optical requests. Check the history, wait, then follow up if nothing moves: the address dedicated to PEC and invoices is in the contact section. Do not deliver the equipment counting on an approval that is not displayed.

The approval is granted, but the payment does not arrive

Start with the history: if the request is still “Validée”, the invoice may not have gone out. If it is “Périmée”, the approval has expired and you need to submit a new request. If it has been “Facturée” for a long time without changing to “Soldée”, write to the PEC and invoices service, quoting the PEC number. Almerys does not publish a payment time on its professional pages.

Keep the exact reason displayed by the portal: it is what tells you what to correct.

When and how does Almerys pay the optician?

Almerys does not publish a payment time specific to optical care on its professional pages. The portal lets you track the file's cycle. “Validée” to deliver, “Facturée” once the invoice is sent, “Soldée” when the file is paid.

The safest method is therefore to track each PEC number until the “Soldée” status. At that point, compare the amount received with the amount displayed when pricing. A discrepancy is handled with the PEC number at hand, with the PEC and invoices service.

On the bank side, reconciling the payments received with the billed files is still done at the store. The principle is the same as for the other third-party payment flows: start from what is expected, reconcile what has arrived, isolate what is missing. Our article on reconciling NOEMIE remittance files and bank transfers details a daily routine that also applies to optical care.

One last point to watch: keep an eye on “Facturée” files that no longer move. A weekly list of billed but unsettled requests, sorted by age, is enough to spot the follow-ups to make before they pile up.

How do you contact Almerys?

The right contact depends on the question. Account and access: the network agreement unit. A file: the PEC and invoices address. Everything else: the healthcare professionals service phone line.

According to the professional portal contact page, network agreement and account questions go to celluleconventionnementalmerys@almerys.com, and PEC and invoice questions to almerys@almerys.com. According to the healthcare professionals page, the healthcare professionals service answers at 0 825 826 214, a premium-rate number. Mail goes to almerys service PS, 46 rue du Ressort, 63967 Clermont-Ferrand Cedex 9.

Before writing or calling, have ready the PEC number, the beneficiary's name as it appears on the card, and the status shown in the history. For a customer complaint, remember that Almerys does not handle complaints from policyholders: direct the customer to their supplementary insurer, whose name is on their third-party payment card.

faqItems.question: How do opticians access the Almerys professional portal?
faqItems.answer: You first need a network agreement: the optician sends a crossed-out claim form or their local health insurance office (CPAM) certificate to the Almerys network agreement unit. The professional portal is on almerys.com, in the healthcare professionals area. The optician then validates their account following the instructions received by email. Logging in requires a login ID, a password, and a 6-digit one-time code sent by email at every login.

faqItems.question: Which supplementary health insurers use Almerys for optical third-party payment?
faqItems.answer: Almerys manages third-party payment on behalf of supplementary insurers: insurance companies, mutuelles, and social protection groups. For example, Aéma Groupe chose it for its mutuelles, including Aésio mutuelle, Apivia Macif Mutuelle, MNFCT, and Math - Prevaris. The portal has no insurer selector: the supplementary insurer appears once the beneficiary is found, and its name is on the customer's third-party payment card.

faqItems.question: How do you submit an optical coverage request on Almerys?
faqItems.answer: The request is made on the Almerys Site des PEC: you find the beneficiary, choose a quote or a coverage request, then enter each item by its LPP code, with the supplier code for lenses. The Valoriser (Price) button creates the request, assigns a PEC number, and displays the amounts. A request covers only one piece of equipment: a second pair needs a second request.

faqItems.question: What do the statuses of an Almerys coverage approval mean (approved, pending, rejected)?
faqItems.answer: The Almerys portal history has eight states: Créée (Created), En instance (Under review), Validée (Approved), Refusée (Rejected), Périmée (Expired), Annulée (Canceled), Facturée (Billed), and Soldée (Settled). Validée means the supplementary insurer accepts the coverage approval and you can deliver, then bill. Créée and En instance indicate a request with no decision. Refusée, Périmée, or Annulée require a new request.

faqItems.question: How do healthcare professionals contact Almerys?
faqItems.answer: The Almerys healthcare professionals service answers at 0 825 826 214, a premium-rate number. Network agreement and account questions go to celluleconventionnementalmerys@almerys.com, PEC and invoice questions to almerys@almerys.com. Almerys does not handle complaints from policyholders: they go to their supplementary insurer.

faqItems.question: How long does Almerys take to pay the optician?
faqItems.answer: Almerys does not publish a payment time specific to optical care on its professional pages. The optician tracks the file in the portal history: Facturée (Billed) once the invoice is sent, then Soldée (Settled) when the file is paid. In case of delay, the optician writes to the PEC and invoices service, quoting the PEC number.
